creator: "The Strip Mills of Trumbull Steel Co.", The Iron Age , February 20, 1919, p. 479
alt: A historical 1919 view of cold-rolling mills at Trumbull Steel, used to illustrate steel manufacturing; this is not a Tata Steel facility.
description: Cold-rolling mills at Trumbull Steel in Warren, Ohio, in the United States in 1919. At left is a single cold-rolling mill, capable of taking cold steel and rolling it into strips 16 inches wide, and anywhere from 0.375 inches in thicknes down to 0.008 inches in thickness. At right are four cold-rolling mills in a line ("tandem mills"), capable of taking cold steel in one, long pass. It can roll cold steel into strips anywhere from 0.5 inches wide to 16 inches wide, and anywhere from 0.375 inches in thicknes down to 0.008 inches in thickness.
caption: A historical 1919 view of cold-rolling mills at Trumbull Steel, used to illustrate steel manufacturing; this is not a Tata Steel facility.
